title: Floating point exception in torch.nn.PixelShuffle

labels.name: module: crash
labels.description: Problem manifests as a hard crash, as opposed to a RuntimeError

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: This issue has been looked at a team member, and triaged and prioritized into an appropriate module

labels.name: module: complex
labels.description: Related to complex number support in PyTorch

labels.name: module: edge cases
labels.description: Adversarial inputs unlikely to occur in practice

body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

python test1.py
```
import torch
print(torch.__version__)
t = torch.zeros((5, 5, 9, 3), dtype=torch.complex32)
input = [
    [545460846592],
    {},
    [t],
    {}
]
r1 = torch.nn.PixelShuffle(*input[0],**input[1])
r2 = r1(*input[2],**input[3])
```
output
```

Floating point exception (core dumped)
```
